create_fft_plan_pair m_cuda_poisson_fft Subroutine

Creates the forward and the backward FFT plan the way the solver does. A backward plan that forces the fallback to plain cuFFT makes the forward plan, built on cuFFTMp, get rebuilt on plain cuFFT, so both plans end on the same library. Shared by the solver init and the x3d2-memcheck probe. The optional arguments are the ones of create_fft_plan. label is appended to the plan names in the messages. When stat is present and not zero, the plans made so far are destroyed and the other plan is left undefined.

R2C with Z-transpose, on (nz, nx, ny). A single rank keeps the plain cuFFT path; on multiple ranks cuFFTMp distributes the transform, and the physical Z-slab is redistributed into its Y-slab input through an MPI_Alltoall (see redistribute_110_to_yslab).

cuda_fft_plan_setup m_cuda_poisson_fft Subroutine

The cuFFT plan dimensions and types of a BC class. The 100 case transposes X<->Y and runs the FFT on (ny, nx, nz), the 110 case transposes to (nz, nx, ny) with R2C along Z, and the 000 and 010 cases run it on (nx, ny, nz). fft_n holds the global plan dimensions and fft_n_loc the local extents of the first two. Shared by the solver init and the x3d2-memcheck probe.

der_penta_periodic m_omp_kernels_dist Subroutine

Cyclic pentadiagonal compact solve via Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury rank-4 correction. A_cyc = A_np + U*W^T where U = [e_1,e_2,e_{n-1},e_n] and W^T encodes the four corner coupling pairs; A_np is the non-periodic Thomas factorisation in (ffr,...).
der_penta_periodic m_omptgt_kernels_dist Subroutine

Cyclic pentadiagonal solve via Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (rank 4): A_cyc = A_np + UC with U = [e_1|e_2|e_{n-1}|e_n]. z holds A_np^{-1}U (see omptgt_tdsops_t%penta_z_dev); each line forms M = I + CZ, solves Mc = Cy and applies y -= Zc.

fft_postprocess_110_cuda m_cuda_poisson_fft Subroutine

Spectral post-processing for 110 case (R2C Z-transpose). Spectral array is (nz/2+1, nx, ny) = (nx_spec, ny_spec, nz_spec). Thread i->X (ny_spec), blockIdx%y k->Y (nz_spec), serial j->Z (nx_spec). On a single rank X and Y are both whole, so 7 kernel launches avoid cross-block race conditions. On multiple ranks cuFFTMp splits X across ranks, so the X pairing reaches its partner through the dim2 mirror exchange (see exchange_dim2_mirror) instead, adding two more launches.
fft_postprocess_110_omp m_omp_poisson_fft Subroutine

Post-process div U* in spectral space for the non-periodic x and y case. After the (nx, ny, nz) -> (nz, nx, ny) transpose applied by fft_forward_110_omp, dim1 holds the periodic z r2c modes, dim2 holds the non-periodic x modes and dim3 holds the non-periodic y modes.

fft_workspace_bytes_query m_cuda_memcheck_device Subroutine

Creates and destroys the forward and backward FFT plans the way the solver does, for the cell dimensions cdims, and for cuFFTMp also the xtdesc buffer, each bracketed with cudaMemGetInfo. worksize_bytes is the plan workspace (used only on the plain cuFFT path, in cuFFTMp it is part of the heap), heap_bytes the memory the plans took, xtdesc_bytes the xtdesc buffer. The 110 BC never uses cuFFTMp. stat is the first non-zero cuFFT/CUDA code, or 0, and the other outputs are then not valid. A plan that aborts inside the library never returns. With query_only set, a cuFFTMp plan is made with auto-allocation off. heap_bytes is then the plan memory without the workspace, worksize_bytes the workspace of both plans (not allocated), xtdesc_bytes is zero and no xtdesc buffer is allocated. A plain cuFFT plan is not changed by it.

field_add_const_x_face_base m_base_backend Subroutine

Adds a uniform constant c to one x-normal face plane of a DIR_X field, in place. Used to enforce exact outlet mass conservation: after the convective outflow update, the outlet-plane mean is shifted uniformly so that it matches the prescribed inlet mean (mirrors Incompact3d's bxxn = bxxn - ut + ut1). at_end = .true. -> the x = nx plane (outlet) at_end = .false. -> the x = 1 plane (inlet)

field_set_face_base m_base_backend Subroutine

A field is a subdomain with a rectangular cuboid shape. It has 6 faces, and these faces are either a subdomain boundary or a global domain boundary based on the location of the subdomain. This subroutine allows us to set any of these faces to a value, 'c_start' and 'c_end' for faces at opposite sides. 'face' is one of X_FACE, Y_FACE, Z_FACE from common.f90 Optionally, bc_start/bc_end select the BC type (default BC_DIRICHLET).

Set a face of f using values supplied by another field f_start. Both fields must be DIR_X VERT pencil-layout. X_FACE uses the inlet plane (pencil index 1) of f_start plus a convective outflow update at the right face. Y_FACE copies the bottom and top y-pencil planes of f_start onto the corresponding planes of f (Dirichlet only).

The 100 and 110 cases pair each dim2 spectral mode with its mirror, which cuFFTMp may place on another rank. Slab index r of P owns global dim2 modes [rm + 1, (r + 1)m] with m = ny_spec, and the mirror of that range is slab P - 1 - r shifted up by one plane, so the extra plane comes from slab P - r. Both partners are symmetric. A single rank holds every partner itself and allocates nothing. This is the only place c_mirror_dev is allocated, see the cuFFTMp check in init_cuda.

outflow_flow_rate_correction m_base_case Function

The flow_rate_diff for the X_FACE stamp of field_set_face_from_field that makes the flow rate out equal the flow rate in exactly, as the pressure projection sees them. The x staggered derivative sums to (u(nx) - u(1))/dx over the cells, so only the two face planes enter, each weighted over y by y_weights: the case passes the weights of the y interpolation (1/2 on a non-periodic boundary plane, 1 elsewhere), with 0 on any plane it overwrites with the same value on both faces after the stamp. The stamp is linear in u, u(nx) <- (1 - c)u(nx) + cu(nx - 1) + flow_rate_diff, so the sums of the planes before it give the outlet flow rate after it. Call it with u as it is about to be stamped, once bc_start_u_x holds this substep's inlet plane. Assumes x is not decomposed, as compute_outflow_params does.

precorrect_walls m_solver Subroutine

Incompact3d's pre_correc: on each Dirichlet face, add the previous projection's tangential correction to the value set by the case. The projection that follows then leaves the face at its prescribed value plus dt(grad p_old - grad p_new), instead of -dtgrad p_new. The kept correction is dt_last*grad p_old, so it is rescaled by dt_now/dt_last first, as Incompact3d does with gdt(itr). The timestep is time_intg_t%stage_dt, the time the substep has advanced from the divergence-free start of the step, which is what the projection scales its correction by. For AB this ratio is always 1; for RK it changes between stages (1/2, 3/4, 1 for RK3). Before the first projection (or after a restart, as in Incompact3d) there is no correction to add.

Multi-rank counterpart of process_spectral_110_x_pair_fw: the X paired split, but the partner mode lives on another rank, reached through the dim2 mirror exchange (see exchange_dim2_mirror). Unlike the single-rank kernel this only updates this rank's own modes; the partner rank updates its own copy the same way. At the global Nyquist mode (even grid size) the mirror partner is this rank's own pre-update value, so the formula below self-pairs it exactly as the single-rank kernel does.

Step 7 (backward): Z periodic undo

x_slice_weighted_sum m_omptgt_kernels_fieldops Subroutine

Sum of the slice f(:, i_slice, :) with the weight w(j) on the points of stacked index j.
x_slice_weighted_sum_base m_base_backend Subroutine

Weighted sum of the x slice f(i_slice, :, :) of a DIR_X field: the point with local y index j counts y_weights(j) times. Gives the flow rate through an x face as the discrete divergence sees it, whose y interpolation weights the boundary planes differently from the interior ones. Caller is responsible for MPI_Allreduce across ranks.

x_slice_weighted_sum_kernel m_cuda_backend Subroutine

Weighted sum of the x slice f(:, i_slice, :) of a DIR_X field, w(j) on the points of y index j. One thread per (y, z) point; z is the fast-varying component of the group index.

y_group_stride m_omp_backend Function

Groups between successive z in the OMP DIR_X ordering, group = stride*(z - 1) + y_block. It is the padded y-block count (see get_index_dir in m_ordering), so it can exceed the number of y-blocks a field uses, e.g. a cell field on a non-periodic y.
Help

Graph Key

Nodes of different colours represent the following:

Solid arrows point from a procedure to one which it calls. Dashed arrows point from an interface to procedures which implement that interface. This could include the module procedures in a generic interface or the implementation in a submodule of an interface in a parent module.

Where possible, edges connecting nodes are given different colours to make them easier to distinguish in large graphs.
